# Are your Dockerfile base images pinned to a digest?

> Paste your Dockerfile and find every FROM line referencing a base image by a mutable tag like node:18 instead of a pinned content digest (@sha256:...). Free, runs in your browser, nothing uploaded.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/docker-base-image-pin-check/)
- [How to pin a Docker base image to a digest](https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/docker-base-image-pin-check/how-to-pin-a-docker-base-image-to-a-digest.html)
- [Docker Base Image Pin Check vs. Hadolint](https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/docker-base-image-pin-check/vs-hadolint.html)
- [Docker Base Image Pin Check vs. reading a Dockerfile by hand](https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/docker-base-image-pin-check/vs-reading-a-dockerfile-by-hand.html)

## How it reads a Dockerfile

- A FROM split across lines with a trailing backslash is read as one instruction; comment and blank lines inside the continuation are skipped, and the finding reports the line it starts on.
- Stage names match case-insensitively, as in BuildKit: `FROM build` after `AS Build` is the stage, not a registry pull.
- `scratch` and earlier stages are left out. A `FROM` built from build args is checked with the `ARG` defaults declared before the first `FROM`; one with no default is reported `unresolved` and counts as a risk.
- A digest needs an algorithm name and hex: exactly 64 lowercase for sha256, 128 for sha512, at least 32 for others.
